overview: White plays an English-like c4 against 2...Nc6, giving a reversed Sicilian-style game. White usually follows with Nc3 and d3 or g3 and Bg2, keeping the centre flexible. Black can play ...Nf6 and ...Bb4 or ...Bc5, ...d6 for a comfortable game.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Nc3, g3 and Bg2 or d3, keeping the centre flexible and aiming for queenside space.
Use c4 to control d5 and prepare a queenside expansion.

black_ideas.idea: Develop ...Nf6, ...Bc5 or ...Bb4 and play ...d6 with a solid centre.
Strike at the centre with ...Nf6 and ...d5 when possible.

typical_structures.structure: Reversed Sicilian with e4/c4 against e5, centre unresolved.

character.notes: A quiet developing set-up with no forcing theory.

structure.notes: Centre is undecided with pawn tension on e4/e5.

approach.notes: Rare for strong players; mostly chosen to avoid theory.
